Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the required fish-control bookshelf and inspect both prescribed wake views before proposing or editing the policy. I’ll keep the policy-specific rationale in the optimization notes and distill only evidence-supported reusable guidance.

The inherited guidance shows a mature lineage: the current parent already captures reliably and its last gain came from phase-allocating an existing terminal residual, not adding steering authority. I’m now checking whether the four sampled rollouts are genuinely distinct and reading the inherited provenance before selecting the strongest finite run and an informative failure.

All four sampled evaluations are byte-identical replications of the same parent candidate and captured rollout, so there is no sampled failure image to contrast. I’ll use the strongest finite capture (the replicated parent) and the inherited failure evidence in `control_experience.md` as the available comparator, and I’ll explicitly treat the missing failure sheet as an evidence limitation rather than inventing visual conclusions. The wake-view skill is now driving the required combined-sheet inspection.

The combined view confirms self-propelled motion from rest: no release-time wake, then an alternating three-dimensional vortex chain develops and remains organized through the long diagonal approach and terminal left hook. The target is reached without a collision-like load event; the metric trace agrees (capture at `24.6400T`, `0.74836L`, low terminal force/moment). Per the bookshelf protocol, I’m now consulting its mechanism index; I’ll transfer only a compact invariant if it addresses the remaining evidenced weakness.

The evidence favors retaining the sampled champion rather than inventing another terminal modifier: all four parent evaluations are identical captures with the best recorded score, and the inherited negatives already falsify broader rate/phase interventions. I’ll make this workspace’s single candidate the existing v41 policy unchanged, and use the new four-sample evidence to strengthen the durable lesson from “one nominal positive” to “deterministically replicated nominal positive,” with an explicit boundary that this still does not prove held-out robustness. No same-worker CFD result will be claimed.

The required notes and durable guidance are now updated; the solver contains exactly one unchanged, evidence-selected v41 candidate. I’m invoking the configured no-CFD check runner now, then I’ll repair any contract, schema, or editable-boundary failure it reports.

The configured runner was invoked but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unsupported on this account—the same infrastructure limitation recorded by prior workers. I’m running its three declared commands directly and separately so the no-CFD validation still completes.

All three prescribed checks pass when run directly, and the additional deterministic schema audit resolves every direct parameter reference (`87/87`) against the returned parameter object. I’m recording that validation in the candidate notes and doing a final scope/hash audit; no CFD has been run.

Completed the Phase 2 candidate:

- Retained the replicated v41 terminal phase-allocation policy as the single candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- Added visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer record, hypothesis, and falsification criteria: [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- Materially revised the reusable lesson with four replicated v41 results: [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:205)

Validation passed:

- Guidance semantic-change check
- Julia public policy contract
- Solver editable-boundary check
- Parameter-schema guard: 87/87 references resolved

The configured runner was invoked but its pinned model was unavailable, so its commands were executed directly. No CFD was run.
